```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Neither federal nor state higher education budgets have kept up with a growing student population and increasingly complex technology.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Public universities and colleges are increasing tuition to the point where young working-class people can no longer afford to attend even community colleges.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Students have been made to finance their education with loans whose high interest profits private lenders, including the newly privatized Fannie Mae.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Highly indebted graduates must choose lucrative jobs over socially useful ones when they even have a choice.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Numerous other advanced industrial nations offer higher education that is low-cost or free.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for increased federal and state support to higher education so that tuition can be radically lowered while shifting financial aid from loans to grants.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Opposition to loans to students from banks or for-profit organizations.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Only when students from all income levels can graduate free of debt will higher education offer social mobility.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
